Nineteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time August 9 2026 Welcome to Fr Theodore Ekwem who will be with us this weekend through Sunday August 23rd During this time I am away on an informal sabbatical to complete my licentiate thesis through the Catholic University of America special Thank you to Fr Theodore for being with us on campus over the next two weeks and for the warm welcome that I know you will show him For any parish needs please contact the Parish Office This weekend Aug 8th 9th the Church celebrates the Nineteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time Immediately after last weeks miracle of the loaves and fishes the disciples find themselves without the Lord and caught in an sudden storm on the Sea of Galilee While they struggle against the wind and waves Jesus comes to them walking on the water reassuring them with the words Take courage it is I do not be afraid Peter steps out of the boat in faith but as soon as he turns his gaze from Jesus to the storm he begins to sink Like Elijah in our first reading who encountered God not in the wind earthquake or fire but in a gentle whisper Peter must focus on the Lord in front of Him and not the storms around him Both he and we are reminded that God is often found not amid the noise of lifes difficulties but in trusting His quiet presence in our lives Over the past several Sundays Jesus has been forming us as His disciples calling us by name teaching us patience and revealing Himself as the greatest treasure we could ever possess This week He teaches us one final lesson discipleship means keeping our eyes fixed on Him especially when the storms of life rage around us Blessed Solanus Casey often reminded people to thank God ahead of time choosing trust before answers came Peter could walk on water only while his gaze remained on Christ So too the more we fix our eyes on Jesus rather than our fears the more we discover that His hand has already been reaching out to us all along Solemnity of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary This coming Saturday August 15th the Church celebrates the Solemnity of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary This is one of our greatest Marian feasts and is ordinarily a Holy Day of Obligation In the United States however whenever the Assumption falls on a Saturday the obligation to assist at Mass is lifted This means that though it is a day of great joy the Solemnity of the Assumption is not a Holy Day of Obligation this year Though not a Holy Day of Obligation this year we can still see the Assumption as a holy day of opportunity You are warmly encouraged to join us as we honor Our Blessed Mother and give thanks to God with two special Mass times vigil Mass on Friday August 14th at 5:30PM and a special morning Mass on Saturday August 15th at 9:00AM Please note both Masses will be offered in the Church Basic Evangelization Training Pope St John Paul II famously declared Now is the time to commit all of the Churchs energy to a New Evangelization But many are left wondering What does that actually look like On Saturday August 22nd we will host St Paul Street Evangelizations Basic Evangelization Training one of the most practical and engaging evangelization workshops available today Whether you are hoping to better share Christ with your children or grandchildren invite a neighbor back to Mass accompany a coworker or simply become more comfortable speaking about our Faith this workshop is for you It will help to equip you with practical methods and tools that can be used in everyday life to confidently share our Faith with joy and charity Jesus final command to the Church was to go and make disciples If youve ever wanted to be more confident in living that mission this workshop is for you Registration is free Please see the event information
